# **Notes**

+   1. you don’t have to remember these netmasks – just look them up as you need them!
+   2. The table rows in **bold** are the default netmasks for class A, B and C networks (Module 4.3)
+   3. these are *all the possible* netmasks (33 of them) and these are the only possible sizes of address range. All the 1-bits are together on the left and all the 0-bits are on the right. If there are any zero bits amongst the 1-bits, it’s not a valid netmask
+   4. ranges are often written as an IP address followed by a “/” and the number of 1-bits in the netmask, i.e. the number of bits in the network part. For example:

192.0.2.181 / 24
